row.category: Vertical SaaS (Healthcare, Education, Real Estate, Construction, Field Service)
row.evidence: athenahealth's help centre has staff user accounts created on the Users page (with an Identity mapping field when domain SSO is used), and SSO is requested through the Customer Success Manager; no SCIM documentation was found.
row.notes: Status changed from none to unknown: the help centre and Okta page show no SCIM, and SSO only maps existing, manually created users, but the API reference (docs.athenahealth.com) could not be loaded (JS portal; headless browser blocked), so the 'none by absence' bar (pricing, docs index, API reference, help centre) is not met. The June price (~$140/provider/mo + 4-7% of collections) and the June claim of a proprietary user REST API had no first-party source and were dropped; the pricing page only says pricing corresponds to the organization's collections. Okta's catalogue page describes federation into athenaNet via Okta org-to-org with no capabilities marked.

plans.name: athenaOne
plans.price_text: Pricing corresponds to the organization's collections (no public price)
plans.notes: Domain SSO is enabled on request through the Customer Success Manager; no plan tiers are published.

limitations.text: Staff accounts are created, updated and deleted on the athenaOne Users page (User Admin role); athenahealth recommends blocking accounts and removing security access instead of deleting them.

okta.notes: OIN page describes federation into athenaNet via Okta org-to-org and tells customers to contact their Customer Success Manager; no SSO or provisioning capability boxes are checked in the page markup.

fallbacks.notes: With domain SSO, admins still create each user on the Users page and enter an Identity mapping value; no just-in-time creation is described. jit=false is inferred from that workflow, not a stated 'no'.
